paper.central_claim: M-star automatically discovers task-optimized memory harnesses by representing a memory harness as an executable Python program (Schema, Logic, Instruction) optimized jointly through reflective code evolution with population-based search; it improves over existing static memory harnesses across all evaluated tasks, and the evolved programs are structurally distinct per task, so every task benefits from its own memory harness.
paper.title: M$^\star$: Every Task Deserves Its Own Memory Harness

evidence.quote: automatically discovers task-optimized memory programs through reflective code evolution.
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim: the edited non-weight object is the memory program (code).

evidence.quote: improves performance over existing static memory harnesses across all evaluated tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Broad claim of improvement on every task.
Columns: LoCoMo F1, L-J, ALFWorld Unseen, Seen, HB Data, Emergency, PR Legal, Finance.
On ALFWorld Seen GEPA+VS 0.820 exceeds M-star 0.700 (also Trajectory Retrieval 0.780): the 'all tasks' claim has a counterexample.

evidence.quote: Table 1 shows that Mstar achieves the highest score on seven of eight reported metrics.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors concede 7 of 8.

evidence.quote: The aggregated score on the static validation set serves as the performance metric for the current memory program.
evidence.support_explanation: Fitness signal: static validation subset (32-60 k-means representative items).

evidence.quote: the generated trajectories on the rotating set are used as feedback to improve the program later.
evidence.support_explanation: Feedback to the coding agent: read/write trajectories and underperforming rotating-set samples.

evidence.quote: we sample a parent program from the pool with probability biased toward higher validation scores.
evidence.support_explanation: Softmax parent selection over a program pool (tau=0.15 per Table 7).

evidence.quote: For each configuration, we run 20 evolution iterations, select the best memory program on validation, and report performance on a held-out test split.
evidence.support_explanation: Retention rule: best-on-validation program reported on held-out test.

evidence.quote: We reserve 100 QA pairs for the held-out test split and use the remaining 1,440 QA pairs as validation data.
evidence.support_explanation: LoCoMo split: test 100, validation pool 1,440; other test sets are 50-100 items (Table 5).

evidence.quote: we construct episode pools from a held-out portion of the benchmark data and keep evaluation queries disjoint from episode construction.
evidence.support_explanation: HealthBench/PRBench episode construction disjoint from evaluation queries.

evidence.quote: gives the largest drop, reducing F1 by 0.203
evidence.support_explanation: Ablation: evolving only instructions (code stays at Vector Search seed) loses 0.203 F1, to 0.256, identical to the Vector Search baseline F1 in Table 1.

evidence.quote: reduces test F1 from 0.459 to 0.318, and Max parent selection reaches 0.381
evidence.support_explanation: Diversity/pool ablation and max-parent ablation on LoCoMo.

evidence.quote: Ablation study on LoCoMo
evidence.support_explanation: All ablations are on one benchmark (LoCoMo) and appear to be single runs.

evidence.quote: Five of six transferred programs perform worse than the universal seed baseline.
evidence.support_explanation: Evolved programs do not transfer; supports task-specificity claim and is also an honest negative result.

evidence.quote: Across the 15 runs, 14 outperform the strongest baseline, supporting consistent gains across initializations.
evidence.support_explanation: Five-seed stability on three benchmarks only.
Seed 0 (=Table 1 headline 0.459) is above the five-seed mean 0.421; one seed (0.364) falls below Mem0 0.373.
Seed 0 again equals Table 1 PR-Finance 0.586, the best of five seeds.

evidence.quote: The total evolution cost ranges from $12–90 per benchmark over 20 iterations
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit cost: $12-90 per run, up to 100 h wall-clock on ALFWorld.

evidence.quote: Computational cost of evolution runs and representative baselines.
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline costs given only for Vector Search and No Memory; the strongest baselines (GEPA, GEPA+VS) are not costed.

evidence.quote: evolution can drift toward task-specific heuristics encoded directly in the program logic
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated limitation; transfer limited.

evidence.quote: we have not measured how strongly the discovered programs depend on this choice
evidence.support_explanation: Single task-agent/reflector model pair; dependence unmeasured.

evidence.quote: We report rubric score, computed as the fraction of criteria marked positive by an LLM judge.
evidence.support_explanation: HealthBench/PRBench scoring uses an LLM judge.

evidence.quote: All experiments use gpt-5.4-mini as the task agent, judge, and toolkit model
evidence.support_explanation: Judge and task agent are the same model; reflector is a stronger GPT-5.3-Codex.

evidence.quote: MemEvolve [ 31 ] searches over four predefined modules (encode, store, retrieve, manage)
evidence.support_explanation: Closest self-evolving-memory neighbor described but not run as a baseline; paper claims to subsume it.

evidence.quote: their search is typically confined to a narrow, designer-specified space
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap about prior memory-harness search.

evidence.quote: the gains are less uniform: Mstar is strongest on open-domain questions and tied on single-hop recall, while Mem0 and GEPA+Vector Search remain stronger on temporal and causal questions.
evidence.support_explanation: Category-level losses on LoCoMo.

evidence.quote: adds a vector database to GEPA because the original GEPA setup does not include a persistent knowledge base
evidence.support_explanation: GEPA+VS is a constructed baseline; GEPA iteration/model budget is not stated.

evidence.quote: any program that still fails after a fixed number of repair attempts is discarded
evidence.support_explanation: Candidate filtering: compile/runtime checks with up to 3 repair attempts (Table 7).

evidence.quote: We provide a set of whitelisted components, including lists, heaps, relational databases, vector databases, and LLM endpoints.
evidence.support_explanation: Search space is bounded by a fixed toolkit; interface Schema/Logic/Instruction is fixed.

evidence.quote: hard items ( finance_hard and legal_hard ) are excluded before train, validation, and held-out test construction to avoid distortion of the fitness signal
evidence.support_explanation: Scope restriction on PRBench; LoCoMo category 5 also excluded.

evidence.quote: The supplementary material includes the anonymized code, experiment scripts, and generated artifacts needed to reproduce the results.
evidence.support_explanation: Code and evolved artifacts in supplement (not inspected).

evidence.quote: We use GPT-5.4 Mini as the task agent and GPT-5.3-Codex as the coding agent in reflective code evolution
evidence.support_explanation: Model pair fixed across experiments.

evidence.quote: The static subset determines fitness, while the rotating subset supplies diverse examples for mutation.
evidence.support_explanation: Static/rotating validation roles.

gap.author_gap: A memory harness that works for one task fails on another, and prior memory-harness search is confined to narrow designer-specified spaces.
gap.checked_gap: Partly supported: the strongest baseline varies by task (Table 1) and M-star's own cross-task transfer fails; but evidence that existing evolvers are limited by their search space (as opposed to budget) is not tested because MemEvolve-style closed-space evolution is not run.
gap.lineage: ReasoningBank/Mem0/G-Memory fixed designs -> GEPA prompt evolution (+vector DB) -> MemEvolve four-module search -> executable memory-program search (this paper); program-evolution lineage via FunSearch/AlphaEvolve-style LLM mutation.
gap.closest_adjacent: MemEvolve (closed four-module space, described, not compared), GEPA (compared, prompt only), ADAS (agent-design search, cited). Another batch paper describes ALMA as meta-learning memory designs as executable code; this paper does not cite it (possible missing nearest neighbor, unverified here).
gap.residue: Per-task schema/retrieval/instruction mismatch of fixed harnesses.
gap.stakes: Strongest fixed baseline differs per task; Mem0 F1 0.373 vs M-star 0.459 on LoCoMo; GEPA 0.449 vs 0.586 on PR-Finance.
gap.method_response: Make schema, logic and instruction a single searchable program and evolve it per task from validation feedback.
gap.remaining_gap: Cross-task transfer, per-iteration cost, dependence on model pair, temporal/causal categories.
unresolved: Whether a MemEvolve-style evolver at matched budget would match M-star
Whether GEPA baselines received comparable iteration budget

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Fixed hand-designed memory harness freed as a searchable executable program evolved by an outer loop and scored by downstream task performance = redesign of the inner learning mechanism.

G.reason: Concrete previously fixed object (hand-designed memory schema/logic/instructions) with measured residual (best baseline varies by task; transfer fails) and named neighbors (MemEvolve, GEPA, ADAS); closest closed-space evolver is not run and the 'subsumes closed spaces' premise is untested.

M.reason: Jointly editing Schema/Logic/Instruction from execution trajectories with validation-based population selection directly targets per-task harness mismatch and gives distinguishable predictions (specialized programs, diversity matters, instruction-only evolution is not enough); the causal role of reflection vs plain mutation is not isolated.

X.reason: Search space, feedback visible to the coding agent, compile/repair gate, parent sampling, fitness subset construction, hyperparameters, retention rule (best-on-validation to disjoint test) and release of programs are reconstructable; boundaries (task-specific drift, no cross-task transfer, category losses, model-pair dependence) are stated.

E.measurement.reason: Standard benchmarks with deterministic token-F1 and ALFWorld success plus expert-written rubrics; rubric scoring uses an unvalidated LLM judge that is the same model as the task agent, and some categories have n=6-9.

E.causality.reason: Ablations (Instruction, Code, parent selection, population) on LoCoMo only and apparently single-run, no random-mutation/no-reflection control, no run of another memory evolver, and evolution compute plus a stronger reflector are not matched to baselines.

E.holdout.reason: Fitness on static validation, reporting on disjoint held-out tests with episode/query disjointness; cross-task transfer reported; deductions for small test sets, no contamination check on frontier models, and an 'all tasks' claim contradicted on ALFWorld Seen.

E.statistics.reason: Five independent evolution seeds with mean/std/CV and win counts on three benchmarks; but baselines and ablations are single runs, no significance test or intervals on 50-100 item tests, and the headline table is the seed-0 run.

E.cost.reason: Per-benchmark calls by role, tokens, dollars and wall-clock reported for the evolution run and for Vector Search/No Memory; GEPA-family baseline costs and matched-budget comparisons are missing.
